source_message.text: In that case, let us mount it vertically.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Choose the orientation that produces the cleanest connector layout, and I will adapt the case to your board.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Regardless of orientation, these are the constraints I can identify:

\- Because the battery sits alongside the PCB, J\_BAT must be on a short edge
\- The user-facing USB-C must also be on a short edge
\- J\_DISP\_SPI / J\_DISP\_I2C / J\_DISP\_LED must be grouped on the edge nearest the display-flex route
\- The antenna end of the ESP32-S3 must face away from the battery and have a ≥8mm keepout

value_updates.usb_c_placement: user-facing USB-C on a short edge
value_updates.display_connector_grouping: J_DISP_SPI, J_DISP_I2C, and J_DISP_LED grouped on the edge nearest the display-flex route
value_updates.esp32_antenna_orientation: antenna end faces away from the battery

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes, I think that should be possible. With only one board plus sensors, buttons, and LEDs that are all easy to position, I do not expect an issue wherever you place the connectors.

value_updates.connector_edge_distribution: the proposed placement along three board sides is acceptable, subject to the identified edge and antenna constraints

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Everything shared looks good except for one potential issue. I think the L-shaped connector above the usb is probably for the battery; because the usb must pass through a case opening, the case would obstruct plugging the battery cable into that connector.

value_updates.battery_connector_accessibility: the battery connector must remain pluggable without obstruction from the enclosure opening around USB-C

source_message.speaker: client

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Because the antenna overhangs the board, the critical keep-out with no copper directly beneath the antenna trace is satisfied. However, J2, CN5, CN17, R14, R19–R21, R25, and S1 are inside the WROOM-1 "recommended antenna clear area." Are you comfortable with the possible slight reduction in WiFi range from leaving those parts in the secondary keepout, or should we try to clear it?

ambiguity.description: It remains unresolved whether components may stay within the ESP32-S3 recommended antenna clear area with a possible WiFi-range reduction or must be moved to clear that area.
